newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian leu closes week stronger.
newsitem.headline: Romanian leu closes week stronger.

text.p: Romania's leu currency closed the week stronger at 6,800/900 to 8,000/100, compared to a Friday opening of 7,000/100 to 8,200/300 on a market still plagued by leu squeezes.
"Dollar supply had been heavy, but few can buy as nobody seems to have leu funds," a dealer said.
Foreign exchange operators expected a further slight strengthening of the leu on the short term.
"With the average one-week rate so high, the leu rush has quickened and the leu has chances to appreciate some more," said a trader.
The average rate on one-week funds at the Romanian central bank (BNR) refinancing auction on Thursday soared to 426.50 percent from 226.35 last week as six banks heavily oversubscribed the BNR offer.
A BNR official said on Friday he did not expect refinancing rates to rise markedly in the next few weeks. The gap between one-week rate and banks' rates would narrow, he said.

"Leu hunger" on the foreign exchange market has increased on Wednesday when the BNR sold dollars to prop up the battered leu. Traders said the BNR sold "several million dollars", but the BNR did not confirm.
"Market liquidity was checked by buying dollars and then selling them," the BNR official said.
"The BNR has not enough foreign exchange reserves to substantially correct the rate of the leu through interventions," he said.
